topics.description: A country in Southern Europe, centered on the Italian Peninsula and including major historical and cultural centers such as Rome and Venice.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this country, the far-right terrorist group Ordine Nuovo carried out the Piazza Fontana bombing, and the far-left Red Brigades kidnapped former PM Aldo Moro, during this country’s Years of Lead [led]. Anti- (*) fascist newspapers like Avanti! were suppressed in this country by a dictator whose corpse was hung upside down. For ten points, name this European country where “Il Duce” [eel DOO-chay], Benito Mussolini, took power after his Blackshirts marched on Rome.
parts.answer: Italy (accept Republic of Italy; accept Kingdom of Italy)

topics.description: The modern Scandinavian sovereign state centered on the Jutland Peninsula and Danish islands, with Copenhagen as its capital and Greenland and the Faroe Islands within the Kingdom of Denmark.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about American holdings in the Caribbean, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This U.S. island territory contains the fort Castillo (cah-STEE-yo) San Cristobal in its capital of San Juan. This territory is often thought to be the most likely candidate for the 51st state.
parts.answer: Commonwealth of Puerto Rico

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The US Virgin Islands were the only Caribbean holding of this Scandinavian kingdom until their sale to the US in 1917. This country’s only current overseas colonies are the Faroe Islands and Greenland.
parts.answer: the Kingdom of Denmark [or Kongeriget Danmark]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A US naval base at this location in Cuba is held in defiance of the Cuban government and has been the site of Geneva Convention-violating torture of enemy prisoners during the War on Terror.
parts.answer: Guantanamo Bay [or Gitmo or the Guantanamo Bay Naval Base or Base Naval de la Bahía de Guantánamo]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The author of the Prose Edda, Snorri Sturluson, was a law speaker of a parliament in this country. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country home to the Althing, so-named to trick people to move to Greenland.
parts.answer: Iceland [accept ĺsland]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In the year 1000, the law speaker Thorgeir Thorkelsson officially decreed that Iceland would undergo this process. Thorgeir threw idols into a waterfall to signal this process. A description is acceptable.
parts.answer: Christianization (accept descriptions involving a conversion to Christianity; prompt on descriptions indicating a rejection of the pagan Norse gods that do not specify a conversion to Christianity)

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Iceland was made Lutheran after its colonization by this Scandinavian country. Greenland is a constituent country of this kingdom, which is governed from Copenhagen.
parts.answer: Kingdom of Denmark [accept Danish Realm]

topics.topic: Kingdom of Denmark under Valdemar IV
topics.description: The medieval Danish kingdom ruled by Valdemar IV Atterdag, including the polity that concluded the Treaty of Stralsund with the Hanseatic League.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Valdemar Atterdag plundered the city of Visby during his war with this organization. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this trade confederation that operated trading posts called kontors in cities like Lübeck. This trade confederation was active in Northern Europe, especially the Baltic.
parts.answer: Hanseatic League [or Hansa]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Valdemar Atterdag was the king of this country that was eventually forced to sign the Treaty of Stralsund with the Hanseatic League. Valdemar was the first king of this country to rule from its current capital of Copenhagen.
parts.answer: Kingdom of Denmark

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Valdemar earlier sold the province of Danish Estonia to this other organization. This organization had previously lost the 1242 Battle of the Ice to the forces of Novgorod under Alexander Nevsky.
parts.answer: Teutonic Knights [or the Teutonic Order or Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem; prompt on the Livonian Order with “what larger organization was it part of?”]

topics.description: Indian politician and prime minister of India who served from 1984 to 1989 and was assassinated by a Tamil Tiger suicide bomber in 1991.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A politician with this surname reversed the decision in the Shah Bano case, which gave a Muslim woman the right to seek alimony from her ex-husband. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Give the surname of that politician, who was implicated in the Bofors Scandal. An earlier politician with this surname was assassinated after ordering the storming of the Golden Temple in Operation Blue Star.
parts.answer: Gandhi [accept Rajiv Gandhi or Indira Gandhi]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Rajiv and Indira Gandhi both served as Prime Ministers of this country. The unrelated Mahatma Gandhi worked with Indira’s father Jawaharlal Nehru to gain this country’s independence from the British Empire in 1947.
parts.answer: India [or Republic of India or Bharat Ganarajya]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] As Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi ruled by decree in a period known as the Emergency, during which her son Sanjay oversaw a campaign of this practice. In the U.S., this practice was the subject of the case Buck v. Bell.
parts.answer: forced sterilization [or mass sterilization; accept descriptive answers; prompt on eugenics]

parts.label: L
parts.question: During this conflict, a group fought to establish an ethnic homeland, in a territory the organization  called “Eelam” (EE-lahm). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this conflict that began in 1983 and was fought between a group led by Velupillai  Prabhakaran (VEL-oo-pil-ai preb-AH-kuh-run) and a government dominated by the Sinhalese (SIN-uh- leez) ethnicity.
parts.answer: Sri Lankan Civil War

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This ethnic group's “Liberation Tigers” fought against the Sinhalese government in Sri Lanka until  its surrender in 2009.
parts.answer: Tamils (TAH-milz) [or Tamilar; or Tamilians; or Tamil Tigers]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Tamil Tigers assassinated Rajiv, an Indian prime minister with this surname. Rajiv was the son  of Indira, another assassinated Indian prime minister with this surname.
parts.answer: Gandhi

topics.description: The major armed struggle in Mexico from 1910 through the 1920s that overthrew Porfirio Díaz and transformed Mexico’s political and social order.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Mariano Azuela’s novel The Underdogs is likely the first novel about this conflict. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this conflict. Ambrose Bierce’s involvement and death in this conflict were fictionalized in The Old Gringo.
parts.answer: Mexican Revolution [or Revolución mexicana]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Mexican author and key figure in the Latin American Boom wrote The Old Gringo. This author detailed the final hours of a veteran of the Mexican Revolution in The Death of Artemio Cruz.
parts.answer: Carlos Fuentes [or Carlos Fuentes Macías]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This real-life bandit and Mexican revolutionary orders the death of General Arroyo in The Old Gringo. Azuela’s The Underdogs drew on his experience working as a doctor for this man, who is known by the nickname “Pancho.”
parts.answer: Pancho Villa [or Francisco Villa or José Doroteo Arango Arámbula]

topics.description: The rigorous state-controlled education and military training system that prepared Spartan boys for citizenship and warfare.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A king of this city died after losing to Epaminondas at the Battle of Leuctra (LEWK-truh). The agoge (AH-goh-gay) system of this city trained children for the military and was invented by Lycurgus. Another king of this city was defeated in battle after a shepherd led the Persian army around the pass at (*) Thermopylae. For ten points, what rival of Athens was home to the famous 300 and was known for its warrior culture?
parts.answer: Sparta

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city’s Gerousia governing body included two jointly-ruling kings. This city’s education system, the agoge [ah-goh-gay], was established by (*) Lycurgus to induct this city’s boys into its army. The helots were a class of slaves in this city, whose king Leonidas was defeated by the Persians at the Battle of Thermopylae. For ten points, name this militaristic Greek city-state that frequently fought with Athens.
parts.answer: Sparta (accept Lacedaemon)

topics.description: A constituent country of the United Kingdom occupying the central and southern portion of the island of Great Britain.

parts.label: L
parts.question: George R. R. Martin is well-versed in medieval history. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The Lannisters and Starks were based on the Lancasters and Yorks, who waged the Wars of the Roses in this  country.
parts.answer: England [or Great Britain; or the United Kingdom]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Aegon the Conqueror’s conquest of Westeros after landing at King’s Landing mirrors this Norman duke’s  conquest of England. This leader won the Battle of Hastings.
parts.answer: William the Conqueror (accept William I)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Martin borrowed elements of his bloody Red Wedding scene from this country’s “Black Dinner.” This country  allied with France in the Auld Alliance.
parts.answer: Scotland

topics.description: The historical kingdom of England that existed before its 1707 union with Scotland to form the Kingdom of Great Britain.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Failure to uphold this document’s Clause Sixty-One led to the First Barons War. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this document that guaranteed certain rights for nobles, as well as a system of balances against the king’s rule. It was signed in 1215 by King John.
parts.answer: Magna Carta Libertatum (accept Great Charter of Freedoms)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Magna Carta was written for this country, which later merged with Scotland to form the Kingdom of Great Britain.
parts.answer: Kingdom of England (do not accept or prompt on “Great Britain”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Magna Carta created the first modern form of this English governing body, which in modern times is made up of the House of Lord and House of Commons.
parts.answer: English Parliament (accept Parliament of England; accept Parliament of the United Kingdom)

topics.description: The British Empire was the worldwide colonial empire ruled or administered by Britain, including territories in Africa and southern Africa.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of this leader’s self-bestowed titles called him “Lord of All the Beasts of the Earth and Fishes of the Seas.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this erratic and allegedly cannibalistic African dictator who overthrew Milton Obote to come to power in 1971.
parts.answer: Idi Amin Dada

parts.label: B
parts.question: Amin faced the Entebbe Raid after he harbored members of the PFLP, who committed this type of crime by unlawfully seizing an airplane.
parts.answer: hijacking [prompt on kidnapping]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Another of Amin’s self-bestowed titles called him the conqueror of this empire, whose former African colonies include Egypt and Sudan.
parts.answer: British Empire [accept United Kingdom or Great Britain] <World History–Kapadia>

parts.label: L
parts.question: The last king of this ethnic group, Cetshwayo kaMpande (thet-shwah-yo kaam-paan-day), was defeated by a colonial army. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this ethnic group, which today is the largest in South Africa. A province of South Africa is named for this ethnic group and Natal.
parts.answer: Zulu people [or amaZulu]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This early 19th century Zulu monarch developed the "bull horn" formation and a shorter style of spear as part of his massive military reformation. The expansion of his realm is argued to have triggered the Mfecane (m-fay-thaa-nay), a long period of social upheaval in southern Africa.
parts.answer: Shaka Zulu [or Shaka kaSenzangakhona]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Zulu Kingdom was eventually defeated by this colonial power, whose armies were also involved in the Boer Wars in South Africa. This country's colonial possessions also included Nigeria, Canada, and Australia.
parts.answer: the British Empire [or the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, or the UK, or Great Britain]

topics.description: An influential ancient Greek city on the Isthmus of Corinth, traditionally founded by Sisyphus and associated with the Isthmian Games, the Corinthian War, and the Corinthian architectural order.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The King's Peace ended a war named for this city that broke out shortly after the Peloponnesian (pel-uh-puh-NEE-zhun) War, which itself followed a dispute between this city and Athens over the colony of Corcyra (kor-SEER-uh). During the spring of the years before and after each Olympic Games, this city hosted the (*) Isthmian (IZTH-mee-un) Games. This city, legendarily founded by Sisyphus (SIS-if-us), names one of the original three Greek orders of columns along with Ionic and Doric. For 10 points, what ancient Greek city's Christian community received two letters from Paul in the New Testament?
parts.answer: Corinth [or Corinthian War; or Corinthian order; or First or Second Corinthians]
